title: Anthropic Details $895.4B Compute Bill With $69.8B Due in a Year as Q3 Swings to Operating Loss

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Anthropic disclosed a multi-decade payment schedule for its $895.4 billion in compute and infrastructure commitments in an amended IPO filing on Monday, detailing that $69.8 billion is due within the 12 months following Sept. 30, $447.5 billion is expected through 2030 and the remainder stretches from 2031 to 2045. Leases signed but not yet started account for $451 billion of the total, including $100 billion signed after Sept. 30, while $214 billion of the obligations carry termination rights or contingent conditions and another $150 billion to $175 billion in deals without fixed dollar amounts sits outside the tally. The filing also showed Anthropic swung to a third-quarter GAAP operating loss of $567 million from a $974 million operating profit in the second quarter, even as quarterly revenue jumped 1,127% year over year and 47% sequentially to $16.96 billion.

The return to an operating loss came as compute and infrastructure expenses rose 78% from the prior quarter to $9.86 billion, lifting compute costs to 58% of revenue and cutting revenue per dollar of compute spend from $2.08 to $1.72. Total third-quarter operating expenses reached $17.5 billion, driven by $5 billion in pricier short-term compute capacity and a $2 billion noncash charge from its employee charitable donation-matching program. Adjusted operating income rose to $2.5 billion from $2.2 billion in the second quarter, though the adjusted operating margin narrowed to 15% from 19%, and Anthropic warned that continued reliance on short-term capacity will further squeeze near-term margins.

Third-quarter net loss widened to $23.3 billion from $12.1 billion a year earlier, including $21.9 billion in noncash revaluation charges on convertible notes, bringing nine-month revenue to $33.2 billion and the nine-month net loss to $104 billion. Operating cash flow for the first nine months was $6.6 billion, up from a $2 billion outflow a year earlier, and Anthropic ended September with $95.6 billion in cash, $36.3 billion in short-term investments, $15 billion in undrawn credit and $13.8 billion in remaining performance obligations. The company also raised its minimum Google Cloud commitment to $121.3 billion through July 2033, granted Alphabet an option to buy up to $10 billion in nonvoting shares at the IPO price, and warned it may imminently reach its internal safety threshold for dramatically accelerated AI-driven research progress.

It included a schedule on the aggregate commitments this time that wasn't filled in the last one. Only ~$70B (8%) in the next 12 months, ~$448B (50%) through 2030, and the remainder (42%) over 15 years from 2031-2045. That's a lot more digestible than the big scary number without any details on near-term binding nature. Still a large number, but there is some flexibility in timing, there. 

$17B quarterly rev so run-rate is ~$68B.

"These commitments represent substantial fixed obligations. As of and subsequent to September 30, 2026, we have entered into purchase commitments and lease agreements, including short-term commitments, as well as leases not yet commenced, with an aggregate committed spend of approximately $895.4 billion, substantially all of which is related to compute and infrastructure. These commitments include approximately $447.5 billion expected to be incurred before December 31, 2030, and substantially all of the remainder is expected to be incurred between 2031 and 2045. Approximately $69.8 billion of these commitments are due in the 12 months following September 30, 2026."

Anthropic published an updated IPO filing today with its third-quarter results for the first time.

> Anthropic went from a $974M operating profit in the second quarter to a $567M operating loss in the third. 

The main causes were $5 B of short-term compute, which costs much more than its long-term contracts, and a $2 B noncash charge for matching employee charitable donations.

> Anthropic swung from a $974M second-quarter operating profit to a $567M loss. Compute rose to 58% of revenue, including $5.0B of pricier short-term capacity, and donation matching added $2B of noncash charges.

> Adjusted operating income still rose to $2.5B from $2.2B, but the adjusted margin fell to 15% from 19%. Anthropic expects to use more short-term compute in the near term, which will squeeze margins further.

> The total compute commitment, left blank in the original, is now $895B. 
Of that, $447B  is expected before the end of 2030, $70B is due within 12 months, and $214B carries termination rights or contingent conditions.

> Leases signed but not yet started make up $451B of the $895B total, and $100B was signed after September 30. Another $150B to $175B in deals without fixed dollar amounts sits outside the total.

> Google’s minimum commitment rose to $121B through July 2033, up from $115B in the October 26 filing, after amendments signed through October.

> Operating cash flow was positive at $7B for the 9 months. Liquidity reached $147B on September 30: $96B cash, $36B short-term investments and $15B of available credit.
